summary: Henry Thoby Prinsep was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Tonbridge School (c. 1805–1807) and East India Company College (1807–1808), and later served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1809 to 1843.

Henry Thomas Colebrooke was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati. He served the East India Company (c. 1782–1814), held judicial and council posts, taught Sanskrit at Fort William College, and was Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (c. 1823–1837).

Henry Thomas Francis worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell (B.A. 1860), he became a Fellow at Gonville and Caius College (1861–1873) and Under-Librarian at Cambridge University Library in 1877.

Henry Thomas Rogers worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1848–1849) and later served as Principal of the College of Engineering, Guindy from around 1869 to 1880.

Henry White Wallis was an Indologist who studied at the University of Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell in 1882. He subsequently served as a Fellow at Gonville and Caius College from around 1886 to 1887.

Henry Whitehead studied at Eton, Oxford, Balliol College, and Princeton. He worked at Buckmaster & Moore (1927–1928), held posts at Balliol College (1932–1941) and the UK Government (1941–1945), and served at the University of Oxford from 1945 to 1960.
Henry Whitelock Torrens was an Indologist who studied at Christ Church, Oxford, completing his B.A. between 1823 and 1825. He later served as Secretary of The Asiatic Society from 1840 to 1846.

Henry William Byerley Thomson studied at University College London and Jesus College, Cambridge. He served as Queen's Advocate of Ceylon at the University of Ceylon in 1858 and as a Puisne Judge at the University of Colombo from 1861 to 1867.

Henry Yule was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at University College London and Addiscombe Military Seminar, later serving on the Council of India (1875–1889) and presiding over the Hakluyt Society and Royal Asiatic Society.
Heramba Chandra Chackravarty was an Indologist who studied under Manindra Mohan Bose. He held a post as a Lecturer at City College, Kolkata, attested in 1977.

Herbert Arthur Popley worked in Indology and religious studies. After earning his B.A. at Hackney College (c. 1898–1901), he served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society from 1901 and worked with the YMCA in 1921.

Herbert Cushing Tolman worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney (Ph.D. c. 1890) and later served as Dean of Arts and Sciences at Vanderbilt University from 1894 to 1923.

Herbert Fletcher De Cou was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Michigan and studied at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens, later serving as an Instructor of Greek and Sanskrit at Michigan (1892–1893).

Herbert Franke studied sinology and Central Asian studies at Cologne, Bonn, Berlin, and SOS, under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer. He served as Professor at the University of Munich (1952–1979) and President of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (c. 1980–1985).

Herbert Frederick Samman was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Emmanuel College from around 1890 to 1893, and later served as a Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Cambridge from 1922 to 1935.

Herbert Galton was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Vienna in 1935 under Nikolai Trubetzkoy and Wilhelm Geiger. He later served as Professor of Slavic Linguistics at the University of Kansas from 1962 to 1988.

Herbert Hope Risley worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Winchester College and New College, Oxford (B.A. c. 1869–1872), and later served as Permanent Secretary of the Judicial Department at the India Office in 1910.

Herbert Härtel specialized in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen, he served as Curator at the Berlin Ethnological Museum (1953–1962), Director of the Museum of Asian Art (1963–1986), and Honorary Professor at Freie Universität Berlin.

Herbert Karl Alfred Plaeschke specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Mode and Karl Ammer, later working as an academic staff member at the University and State Library of Saxony-Anhalt from around 1959 to 1993.

Herbert Leonard Offley Garrett was an Indologist and historian who studied at St John's College (c. 1899–1902). He taught at Queen's College, served as Principal of Government College University, Lahore (1927–1936), and was a Syndic of the University of the Punjab.
